summary.intent: Resolve all open PR review comments on PR #372 from automated reviewers (GitHub Copilot), triaging each comment and implementing valid fixes.
summary.outcome: 4 of 5 threads had fixes implemented (3 valid fixes + 1 not applicable), tests passed, and changes were committed and pushed. Thread replies and resolutions were also posted.

repo: ShareKeyEntryDtoKeyType already includes 'folder-ipns' as a valid key type — Copilot incorrectly flagged this as missing.
The shares system distinguishes between file-ipns and folder-ipns key types; downgrade and write-recipient logic must handle both.
FilePointer.id uses shareId but key lookup matches on itemId — these are distinct identifiers in the share model.
SDK integration tests require a live API and are expected to fail in local/CI environments without credentials.

code.finding: FilePointer.id holds shareId but the key lookup needs itemId — using the wrong field causes key resolution failures for shared files.
Comment claimed a fallback existed but no fallback was implemented — comment was misleading and was corrected.
Write recipients could add folder-ipns keys, which should be blocked — fixed with an explicit key type guard.
Share downgrade only deleted file-ipns keys, leaving folder-ipns keys behind — fixed to delete both types.

workflow: TypeORM's In() operator must be explicitly imported when added to a query — easy to miss when editing existing service files.
gh api GraphQL resolveReviewThread mutation can batch multiple thread resolutions in one call.
REST comment replies require --field (not -f) for in_reply_to and the value must be an integer, not a string.

friction: Required multiple grep/read passes to understand the shareId vs itemId distinction before being confident in the fix.
Needed to verify ShareKeyEntryDtoKeyType manually to correctly mark thread 3 as not applicable rather than accidentally implementing a duplicate fix.
TypeORM In() import was missing after editing shares.service.ts and required a separate read+edit pass to fix.
open_items: SDK integration tests are skipped locally due to requiring a live API — no local mock or test harness exists for these.
The shareId/itemId confusion in SharedFileBrowser.tsx may indicate a broader naming inconsistency in how share identifiers are passed through the file browser component tree.
